title: The Round Fort and the Casa Mare: Seven Slow Days in Small-Town Moldova
subRegion: The Middle Dniester, Soroca, and the Orhei Codru

bestPeriod.window: the second half of May into mid-June, then all of September
bestPeriod.avoid: mid-July to late August (35 °C, dust, no shade); February-March, when the thaw turns every unsealed village street to axle-deep clay

food.note: €75, €130 (€11, €19/day, most meals are cooked by your host, not bought)

transport.note: €160, €250 (small hire car from Chișinău plus fuel; roughly 700 km driven)

activities.note: €25, €55 (fortress and museum entries, monastery donations, a guide at Orheiul Vechi)

hook: Two towns, six nights split between them, and a lot of sitting down. Soroca has a perfectly circular fifteenth-century fort on the Dniester, six hundred steps up a cliff to a stone candle, and a hillside of self-built mansions copying the Bolshoi Theatre. Orhei has a limestone canyon and villages where the front room is still kept empty for guests. You eat what the household grew, in the house, because there is no restaurant. That is the point.

snapshot.Best period: Mid-May to mid-June; all of September
snapshot.Getting there: Chișinău International (KIV), 13 km southeast of the centre. Hire a car at the airport, rural buses run to school and market timetables and will not fit this route. Trolleybus 30 into town is 7 MDL; a Yandex Go or Bolt car lands around 160 MDL (€8). Iași, in Romania, is 3 h by road.

itinerary.title: North to the Dniester
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at KIV and leave Chișinău before the school run. The M2 north through Orhei is the good road; the last stretch into Soroca via Florești is patched but sound.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop bags and walk down Strada Independenței to the river. The Dniester is wide, brown and slow here, and the far bank is Ukraine, the village opposite is Tsekinivka. There is no crossing.
itinerary.evening: Join the promenade on Piața Unirii around 18:30. Eat in town tonight; from tomorrow the cooking is domestic.

itinerary.title: The perfect circle and the six hundred steps
itinerary.morning: **Soroca Fortress**, founded in 1499 by Ștefan cel Mare as a timber fort over the Dniester crossing and rebuilt in stone by Petru Rareș in the 1540s. A true circle, roughly 37 m across inside, four round bastions and a square gate tower, among the best-preserved medieval round forts in Europe. Restored in 2015; the wall gallery and towers are open.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb to the **Candle of Gratitude** (Lumânarea Recunoștinței), the stone candle-tower raised in 2004 on the cliff at the initiative of the writer Ion Druță, for the anonymous chroniclers who kept the language written. The stair from the riverside is usually given as about six hundred steps: steep, unshaded, worth it. Late afternoon for the light down the gorge.
itinerary.evening: Buy tomorrow's picnic at the market before it shuts, then dinner at the guesthouse.

itinerary.title: Roma Hill, then the northern park
itinerary.morning: **Dealul Țiganilor**, Roma Hill, rises behind the centre. From the 1990s, Soroca's Roma families, one of the largest such communities in Moldova, built houses quoting whatever they admired: a near-copy of the Bolshoi Theatre, a white-domed version of Sacré-Cœur, echoes of St Peter's and of Moscow apartment blocks. Many are unfinished and many stand empty, because the money that built them is earned abroad. **This is a residential neighbourhood, not an attraction.** Walk the streets, stay out of yards, ask before photographing anyone, never photograph children, and arrange any interior visit through your guesthouse rather than knocking.
itinerary.afternoon: North to **Țaul**, Dondușeni district, for **Parcul Țaul**, at roughly 46 hectares the largest landscape park in Moldova, laid out around 1901 for the landowner Andrei Pommer, with a manor, terraced ponds and a couple of hundred introduced tree species now grown enormous.
itinerary.evening: Stop in **Dondușeni**, a quiet railway town with a good bakery on the main street, then back to Soroca in the last hour of light. Watch for cattle on the R7.

itinerary.title: Down the river to Orhei
itinerary.morning: South along the Dniester through **Cosăuți**, whose sandstone quarries supplied the stone for half the monuments in the country.
itinerary.afternoon: **Rezina** sits directly opposite **Râbnița** on the left bank, inside the Transnistrian de facto administration; the bridge between them is a controlled crossing. Look at it from the Rezina side and do not drive over, a hire car's insurance will not follow you. Continue south on the R20.
itinerary.evening: Through Orhei and on to **Butuceni** in the Răut canyon, 18 km further. Settle in, eat at the long table, sleep with the window open.

itinerary.title: Orheiul Vechi
itinerary.morning: The **Orheiul Vechi Cultural-Natural Reserve**: a white limestone meander of the Răut with a **cave monastery** cut into the cliff and reached along a ledge, and the Church of the Ascension of St Mary (1905) on the ridge above. Entry **20 MDL** adult, 10 MDL students and pensioners; the Butuceni information point runs 08:00-18:00 weekdays, 08:00-20:00 weekends. A guide for one to ten people is **200 MDL in Romanian, 300 MDL in English, Russian, French or Italian**, about 90 minutes, and worth it.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the village, the ethnographic house, the stone walls, the *fântână* with its windlass, wine cellars cut into the slope, then up to the **Belvedere** platform on the Trebujeni side (09:00-17:00 Wed-Fri, 09:00-18:00 weekends) for the whole meander in one frame.
itinerary.evening: The best food of the week: *zeamă*, *plăcinte* with brânză and dill, *sarmale* in vine leaves, house wine out of a plastic bottle that is better than it looks.

itinerary.title: The Codru craft loop
itinerary.morning: West on the ridge road through **Peresecina**, down into the Codru to **Bahmut**, a walnut-and-orchard village in a wooded valley in Călărași district and one of the prettiest short drives in the country. Then **Călărași** for the market, where the Iurceni willow-workers' baskets actually turn up for sale.
itinerary.afternoon: **Hoginești**, 15 km on, for pottery. Ring ahead through your guesthouse; the working households are not signposted and a cold call rarely finds a kiln hot. With appetite for another 45 km south, **Iurceni** in Nisporeni district is the willow village itself.
itinerary.evening: Back over the ridge as the light goes. Cattle come home between 18:00 and 19:30 on all of these roads and they own them. Drive at 40.

itinerary.title: A manor, a market, and out
itinerary.morning: Orhei's *piața* early, for walnuts, dried fruit, sunflower halva and a jar of honey.
itinerary.afternoon: **Ivancea**, 12 km south on the Chișinău road: the nineteenth-century **Balioz manor** in its park of introduced trees, now the **Museum of Folk Crafts**, a branch of the National Museum of Ethnography and Natural History, carpets, pottery, cooperage and ironwork laid out in the rooms.
itinerary.evening: On to Chișinău, 46 km. Return the car and eat at a table you did not have to warn anybody about.

accommodationStrategy.name: Casa Părintească
accommodationStrategy.description: the original Butuceni guesthouse and still the standard, a restored traditional house with a proper *casă mare*, wall carpets, a masonry stove and a kitchen cooking from the garden. Five minutes from the canyon path, so you reach the cave monastery before the first minibus.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct by phone, or through moldovaholiday.travel; 3-4 weeks ahead in May and September, longer for the first weekend of October, when Wine Day empties the whole Orhei area.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Central
accommodationStrategy.description: plain, warm and walkable, ten minutes from both the fortress gate and the Candle stair, with parking off the street, which matters here. It puts you inside the evening promenade rather than in a village 20 km out.
accommodationStrategy.booking: Booking.com or direct, a week ahead; Soroca only fills for weddings and the September town day.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hanul lui Hanganu
accommodationStrategy.description: the swap for anyone who would rather sleep on the Dniester than in a town, stone-and-timber houses under the cliffs, boats, a wood-fired kitchen, almost no phone signal. Slots into Day 4 if you want to split the relocation across two nights.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct, and confirm dinner when you book, there is nowhere else to eat within 15 km.

logistics.connectivity: Orange and Moldcell cover every town and most villages; 4G in Soroca, Orhei and Călărași is good. A prepaid SIM costs under €5 and needs your passport. Signal drops in the Răut canyon at Butuceni and along the Dniester below Lalova.
logistics.emergency: **112**, answered in Romanian and Russian and usually in English. Rural ambulances come from the district hospital and can be 40 minutes out. Pharmacies in Soroca and Orhei are well stocked; villages have none.
logistics.weather: Continental and blunt. May and September run 18-25 °C with cold mornings. A summer thunderstorm can drop 40 mm in an hour and close an unsealed village road for a day, nothing here is dangerous, but swap the lane for the sealed R-road and lose nothing.
logistics.bookingWindows: Guesthouses 2-4 weeks ahead in shoulder season, 6-8 weeks for the first weekend of October. Ring the day before to reconfirm and order dinner; small *pensiuni* do not read email daily.
logistics.money: Roughly 19-20 MDL to €1. Cards work in district-town supermarkets and larger guesthouses and nowhere else. Draw cash at a Maib or Victoriabank ATM and carry small notes, markets, monasteries, hosts and potters are all cash. Change euro at a *casă de schimb*, never on the street.
logistics.transportRules: Headlights on at all times, day and night, mandatory. Limits are 50 km/h built-up, 90 outside. Alcohol is effectively zero-tolerance. A first-aid kit, warning triangle and fire extinguisher must be in the car; check all three before leaving the airport.
logistics.permits: No permits for anything here. Orheiul Vechi charges the 20 MDL reserve entry. Monasteries take donations, not tickets; cover shoulders and knees, and women cover their heads inside the church, scarves are lent at the door. Antique carpets, icons and coins are protected cultural property and cannot legally leave the country.

proTips: **Order dinner at breakfast.** Village hosts shop to order. Say *"cină pentru două persoane, vă rog"* in the morning and you get a feast; say it at 19:00 and you get eggs.

**Do Roma Hill on foot and early.** The 09:00-10:00 window is when the neighbourhood is awake and least bothered by a quiet stranger with no camera raised. Arrange any interior visit the night before, through your host, and take a gift rather than offering cash first.

**Climb the Candle from the bottom.** There is a road to the monument, but the cliff stair from the river is the experience, and the last flight opens onto the Dniester all at once. Come down by the road if your knees object.
**Four words.** *Bună ziua*, *mulțumesc*, *cât costă?*, and *poftim*, which means help yourself, here you are, and after you, and which you will hear forty times a day.
**Buy the carpet from the loom.** A new *covor* costs a fraction of the Chișinău gallery price and the money stays in the house. Ask your host who is weaving; there is always someone.
**Reverse the day.** Moldovan markets die by noon and Moldovan monuments are best in late-afternoon light. Build every day that way round and you queue for neither.

**Take the R-road, not the shortcut.** Your navigation app will route you down a *drum de țară* to save 6 km. Dry, it is a pleasure. An hour after rain it is a clay trap, and there is no recovery service.

raw.Squares and centres by name: **Soroca's Piața Unirii**, the shallow square between the Casa de Cultură and the river, where the town walks between 18:00 and 20:00 and nobody is going anywhere; **Strada Independenței** runs downhill from it to the fortress gate. **Orhei's Piața Vasile Lupu**, with the Sfântul Dumitru church (1636, Vasile Lupu's foundation) at one end. **Butuceni's single unpaved street**, white limestone dust, stone-walled yards and vine pergolas, following the Răut meander. **Călărași's market square**, the most workaday and the most rewarding of them.
raw.Market days and artisan specialities: The *piața* is the timetable. **Soroca's central market** off Strada Ștefan cel Mare works daily but empties by 11:00; growers come in from Vasilcău and Cosăuți on **Wednesday and Saturday**. **Orhei's piața** is strongest **Thursday and Sunday**. Village fairs (*iarmaroc*) follow a commune calendar, not a tourist one. Craft: **Hoginești** in Călărași district is the surviving red-clay pottery village of the central Codru, where a few households still throw and wood-fire glazed *ulcioare*; **Iurceni** in Nisporeni district is the willow village, where families cut and steam *lozie* and weave baskets, panniers and fish traps. And *covor moldovenesc*, the flat-woven, weft-faced Moldovan wall carpet, inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List in 2016 jointly with Romania. Old carpets are protected cultural property and cannot be exported; buy new, from the weaver.
raw.The casa mare: Every traditional house has one, the "big room" facing the road, unheated and unused all year, kept for guests, weddings and wakes. It holds the dowry textiles, the wall carpets, the icons in the eastern corner, the good bed nobody sleeps in. In a village *pensiune* you will often be given it. It is the household's status object; admire the carpets out loud.
raw.Stays, honestly: There is no boutique-hotel sector here. What exists is a rural guesthouse network, several hundred registered *pensiuni*, promoted through **moldovaholiday.travel**, the portal run by ANTRIM, the national inbound tourism association, and through Booking.com for the larger ones. Standards run from farmhouse-with-outside-tap to properly restored stone house.
raw.One relocation, mid-week: **Soroca nights 1-3 → Butuceni/Orhei nights 4-6 → Chișinău night 7**: a single 135 km move on Day 4, taken slowly down the Dniester. Everything else radiates from a base. Day-trip legs: Soroca-Țaul 55 km (1 h 10), Soroca-Rezina 85 km (1 h 45), Orhei-Călărași 65 km (1 h 20), Orhei-Ivancea 12 km (15 min).
raw.Meals are arranged, not found: Outside Soroca, Orhei and Călărași most villages have **no restaurant at all**, a *magazin* selling bread, sausage and beer is the extent of it. Tell your host at breakfast whether you want dinner. Expect €5, €8 (100-150 MDL) a head, cash, and expect to be over-fed.
